title: All data lives in each user's browser; nothing is shared or stored centrally
what: State is read from and written to localStorage under one key; there is no server or database.
business_impact: The team cannot work on one board, and a cleared browser loses all tasks for that person.
fix: Add a small API and database for tasks, categories and settings; keep the current UI.

title: The admin role is self-selected at sign-in
what: The role comes from a drop-down the user fills in; there are no accounts or passwords.
business_impact: Anyone can change categories and the delete rule, so permissions give no real control.
fix: Introduce real accounts with roles assigned by an administrator, checked on the server.

title: Permissions are enforced only in the browser
what: Settings and Delete are hidden by the page itself; the delete handler does not re-check the permission.
business_impact: Once data is shared, a user could bypass the delete rule; today it only affects their own copy.
fix: Check permissions on the server for every change once an API exists.

title: No backup, restore or import
what: The only way out is a CSV export; there is no way to load tasks back.
business_impact: Lost or wiped browsers mean permanently lost work.
fix: Server-side storage with daily backups; add CSV import.

title: All logic in one file with no separation of concerns
what: State, rendering, routing and events share one 109-line closure.
business_impact: Small today; new features will get slower and riskier to add as the file grows.
fix: Split into state, view and API modules when the server is added.
